structural: `requirements.sdk.domain` has two structural obligations. First, `trust_but_verify::domain::Domain` must be a trait with the exact quoted shape. Second, it must carry the supertraits `Clone + Send + Sync`, which are the text's "cloneable and safe to share between executions". An alternative could keep the same runtime behavior while dropping a supertrait bound, replacing the trait with a struct, or changing a member signature. Any of those would violate the text, so these clauses are not discretionary.

The root `crates/trust-but-verify/src/domain.rs#trait[Domain]` carries the {impl} marker and matches the text.

- **Supertraits:** `pub trait Domain: Clone + Send + Sync`.
- **Associated types, bounds as quoted:**
  - `Error: Send`
  - `NodeData: Clone + Eq + Hash + Send + Sync`
  - `NodeContent: NodeContents`
  - `EdgeLabel: Clone + Send + Sync`
- **Required methods:**
  - `cache(&self) -> &ValidationCache<Self>`
  - `node_path(&self, &NodeId<Self>) -> NodePath`
  - `node_content(&self, &NodeId<Self>) -> Result<Self::NodeContent, Self::Error>`
  - `outgoing_edges(&self, &NodeId<Self>, Self::EdgeLabel) -> Result<Vec<NodeId<Self>>, Self::Error>`
  - `load_evidence(...) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Option<Record<NodeData, EdgeLabel>>, Error>> + Send`
  - `store_evidence(..., &Record<...>) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), Error>> + Send`
- **Defaulted methods:**
  - `project_sources(&self) -> Option<SourceProject<Self>>`
  - `source_node(&self, &OutlineData) -> Result<Self::NodeData, SourceError>`
  - `source_address(&self, &Self::NodeData) -> Option<OutlineData>`

I read each of these items in the trait's children and checked them against the quoted declaration. They agree.

The sentence "Every application domain implements `Domain`" is satisfied by the trait's existence, since the application supplies each implementation. The text names no other structural obligation for this root, such as a required library or algorithm. The chapters that introduce individual members are refined by other requirements, which the member-level markers reference.

No gap.

behavioral: `requirements.sdk.domain` states three things. Every application domain implements `Domain`. A domain is cloneable and safe to share between executions. The member signatures are introduced and tested by later chapters.

- **Trait implementation and bounds.** Rust enforces `Clone + Send + Sync` and the associated-type bounds when the trait is implemented. Every marked test uses a domain type that implements `Domain` (`Memory`, `Application`, `Relationships`). `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/contracts.rs#fn[domain_relationships_accept_opaque_types_and_send_only_errors]` also checks the bounds. It runs `check_bounds` and asserts that `load_evidence` and `store_evidence` futures are `Send`. It also covers opaque `NodeData` and send-only errors.
- **Safe to share between executions.** Several marked tests run concurrent executions against one shared domain and assert that they stay independent.
  - `src/agent/tests.rs#fn[concurrent_tool_agents_isolate_histories_pages_and_submissions_and_share_reads]` runs two concurrent tool agents on one graph.
  - `src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[shared_context_allows_independent_concurrent_agent_calls]` and `#fn[concurrent_single_node_validations_keep_separate_traces]` run concurrent agent calls and validations on one graph. The second asserts separate traces and records.
  - `tests/contracts.rs#fn[concurrent_same_criterion_executions_keep_complete_independent_records]` runs two executions of the same criterion on one `Application`. It asserts complete, independent records.
- **Cloneability.** This is a compile-time bound. Tests elsewhere clone domains, such as `domain.clone()` in `src/agent/configured.rs`. They aren't marked for this requirement, but the bound can't be met without `Clone`, so this isn't a behavioral gap.
- **Default members.** `project_sources`, `source_node` and `source_address` are covered by `tests/contracts.rs#fn[domain_without_project_sources_leaves_source_tools_disabled]`. Their detailed behavior is also tested through the refining requirements.
- **Supplied contents.** `src/sdk.rs#mod[tests]/fn[domain_formats_supplied_contents_without_resolving_a_replacement]` covers formatting of supplied contents.
- **Delegated members.** The trait's members are introduced one capability at a time in later chapters. Their obligations belong to those requirements, which have their own tests.

I found no behavioral obligation here that lacks a test.
